question: Should OpenClaw add a native ASR/STT backend abstraction now, and if so which first slice owns provider scope, credential isolation, private-network policy, and fallback behavior?
rationale: Current code proves the capability is missing, but the safe implementation shape crosses native apps, Gateway/provider contracts, settings, secrets, and privacy/security policy.

options.title: Design shared seam, start with macOS PTT
options.body: Use #87140 as the first narrow slice, preserving Apple Speech by default while defining a reusable native STT backend contract and credential policy.

options.title: Build broad cross-platform settings
options.body: Add ASR provider settings across macOS, iOS, Android, and WebChat in one larger project, accepting more design and upgrade risk up front.

options.title: Defer native ASR core work
options.body: Keep self-hosted STT limited to existing tools.media.audio, Talk relay, channel, or sidecar paths until maintainers prioritize native-app extension points.

recommendation.title: Design shared seam, start with macOS PTT
recommendation.body: Use #87140 as the first narrow slice, preserving Apple Speech by default while defining a reusable native STT backend contract and credential policy.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is tied to the native Talk/macOS voice feature history and is a likely product-scope owner for deciding the first native-app slice.
